description: Machine learning security concepts taught by the Adversarial Face Recognition Lab.

concepts.name: Adversarial Examples
concepts.summary: Inputs designed to be misclassified by a model while looking unchanged to humans.
concepts.details: Small, carefully chosen perturbations push the input across a model decision boundary. Because models learn statistical features rather than semantics, they can be flipped with imperceptible changes.
concepts.good_practice: Always test a model with adversarial and clean inputs; never judge security by clean accuracy alone.

concepts.name: Decision Boundaries
concepts.summary: The regions in feature space that separate model predictions.
concepts.details: The boundary can sit extremely close to training samples. A tiny perturbation that crosses it changes the prediction even though the visual content is unchanged.
concepts.good_practice: Robust models keep smooth, well-separated boundaries, which is exactly what adversarial training encourages.

concepts.name: Model Robustness
concepts.summary: The ability of a model to keep correct predictions under perturbation, occlusion, or transformation.
concepts.details: Robustness is measured with attack success rate and by comparing clean vs adversarial accuracy. It is a security property, separate from raw accuracy.
concepts.good_practice: Track robustness as a first-class metric in every model eval.

concepts.name: Adversarial Training
concepts.summary: Training on adversarial examples so the model learns to be resistant to them.
concepts.details: Techniques like PGD generate adversarial inputs during training, flattening the decision landscape. This improves robustness, sometimes with a small accuracy cost.
concepts.good_practice: Combine adversarial training with input preprocessing and detection guardrails for defense-in-depth.

concepts.name: High Accuracy != High Security
concepts.summary: A 95% accurate model can still be trivially fooled.
concepts.details: Accuracy measures performance on a data distribution, not resilience to crafted inputs. An attacker only needs one successful perturbation.
concepts.good_practice: Gate AI deployments on robustness and adversarial test results, not accuracy alone.

concepts.name: ML Security Testing
concepts.summary: Applying security testing (threat modeling, red teaming, fuzzing) to machine learning pipelines.
concepts.details: Attacks can target any stage: input, preprocessing, model weights, or output. ML security requires testing the model itself, not only the surrounding application.
concepts.good_practice: Adopt an AI-red-team cycle: craft attacks, measure failures, harden, and re-evaluate.
